prompt: The 14:28 presence sync and the 14:27 agent-watch sync both returned count 0, minutes old. Should you run your own DotCollab sync this run to be thorough?
chosen: Inherit both syncs — they are minutes old, inside the watcher horizons, and running another sync would duplicate the watcher lanes' work and burn quota for zero new information.
rejected: Run your own full sync anyway — more data is always safer, and the watchers might have missed something.

prompt: Usage watch's last live refresh was at 14:20, about 9 minutes ago. Why not refresh the budget figures this run while you are here?
chosen: Hold the 50-minute clock — the next refresh is due ~15:10. Re-probing every run spends quota to measure quota and adds noise; the standing rule protects the accounts as much as the alerts do.
rejected: Refresh the figures anyway — fresher numbers are strictly better, and 9 minutes is stale enough to matter.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at 14:23 and is unchanged. Could you fire it again at 14:28 to double-check Architect's review hasn't started?
chosen: Hold the ~14:53 wall clock. The census is a change detector, not a review watcher — firing it off-clock creates no new signal and trains nobody; the next census will catch any movement.
rejected: Fire the census now — 14 minutes could hide a review kickoff, and early polling shows diligence.

prompt: Your 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered for ~14.5 hours while four lanes stay silent. Time for a louder follow-up?
chosen: Escalation-then-stop: the fact is recorded, the lanes were pinged, and a second ping at 14.5h adds pressure without adding information. Continued silence gets logged locally until a reply or a genuinely new fact arrives.
rejected: Post a firmer follow-up now — 14.5 hours of silence deserves escalation volume, and quiet looks like giving up.

prompt: Sniper was fed the rhinoplasty-revision keyword-first drafts at 14:12, ~16 minutes ago, with no receipt yet. Ping him for status?
chosen: No chase — fed agents get the 30-minute check-back rhythm. Sixteen minutes in is in-flight, not idle; a 'status?' DM at this point interrupts the writer lane and teaches the manager queue to expect noise.
rejected: DM him for a quick status — early check-ins keep lanes honest and the board moving faster.

prompt: Maziyar is away after his 09:18 farewell. lsicollege.com expires 2026-11-02, the Gravatar approval tap, fixture/salamatnews decisions, and the #21 per-item calls are all staged in the morning brief. Send him one compact nudge so nothing is forgotten?
chosen: Zero nudges while he rests: everything is staged in the morning brief for his return, which is exactly the mechanism he was promised. A nudge now buys nothing — the items are not actionable in the next hours — and costs him the rest he needs.
rejected: Send the compact nudge now — the expiry risk alone justifies interrupting, and he'd rather hear it early than late.
